evidence: Sen. Ep. 72.8: quidquid excēpit prōtinus integrum dēvorat
Cato Agr. 99: fīcī āridae sī volēs utī integrae sint
terms.comment: From in- and the root of tangō: “untouched” (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plin. NH 8.36: ut solidōs hauriant cervōs taurōsque (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 6.253: solida taurōrum vīscera (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First of all “solid, not hollow”; “whole” as opposed to divided.

phrases.latin: vīdistī aliquandō canem missa ā dominō frusta pānis aut carnis apertō ōre captantem? quidquid excēpit prōtinus integrum dēvorat
phrases.english: have you ever seen a dog snapping open-mouthed at the scraps of bread or meat its master throws? whatever it catches it swallows whole at once

phrases.latin: fīcī āridae sī volēs utī integrae sint, in vās fictile conditō
phrases.english: if you want dried figs to keep whole, put them away in an earthenware jar

sources: Lewis & Short: integer · Lewis & Short: solidus
